items.excerpt: An exclusive look inside Google's plan for the AI glasses it and Samsung will ship this fall — the designs, the privacy backlash it wants to avoid, and how it intends to fight Meta and Apple for a place on your face.
Google is baking anti-tampering protections for the recording indicator into Android XR from day one, saying privacy and trust — not optics or AI — are the biggest hurdles facing smart glasses.
OpenAI's first shipping hardware turns out to be the Codex Micro, an RGB macropad with 13 low-profile keys and a joystick built to dispatch and steer AI coding agents from a physical control surface.
OpenAI's $230 Codex Micro, made with Work Louder, is a programmable keypad for bossing around AI agents — mechanical switches, a joystick, and illuminated keys that show live agent status.
Review of the Asus ROG Xreal R1: gaming-focused AR glasses with a 240 Hz display and RGB styling, positioned as the best wearable display for the gaming crowd.
1X's Neo Beta home robot shows off new hands that can assemble LEGO, unzip a jacket and open a snack bag — the most human-like manipulation yet from a consumer humanoid.

The Signal Ring, from an ex-Google health lead, drops sleep scores and step counts entirely to chase one thing: cuffless, calibration-free blood pressure sensing that Apple and Samsung haven't cracked.
Oura Ring 5 review: Oura didn't reinvent the smart ring this year, but a slimmer build and refined AI advisor make it the first one that feels like jewelry you'd actually buy.
VITURE Beast review: the XR glasses fix nearly everything that held back the Luma Pro for $50 more, and are the first pair the reviewer wants to travel with.
nubia unveils the NaviX Ultra, its take on the 'AI agentic phone' — the concept Chinese phone makers are racing to define, with an on-device agent driving the whole UI.
Hands-on with the Viaim RecDot AI earbuds, which record, transcribe and summarize meetings in real time — an AI hearable that doubles as a note-taker.
Palmer Luckey quietly teased a strikingly compact pair of unannounced Anduril AR glasses — not just smart glasses, he says, but built for full AR.
XREAL's new 'X by Xreal' sub-brand brings its first budget XR glasses out of China: the xbx a01+ lands in the US at $300 via Amazon, Best Buy, B&H and Micro Center.
The European Commission is moving to exempt smart glasses and other wearables from the EU's user-replaceable battery rules — a legislative tweak that keeps sealed AI glasses shippable in Europe.
The 18Birdies and Arccos apps now plug into Meta AI on Ray-Ban glasses in the US and Canada, turning the wearable into a hands-free AI golf caddy that reads the hole and recommends clubs.
Per the FT, Meta is still internally debating how to handle the privacy LED on its next glasses with always-on AI — a design decision that defines whether continuous capture is socially acceptable.
Gemini for Home is redesigning its visual answers on Nest Hub and Smart Displays, starting with weather and knowledge cards — the assistant's screen UI being rebuilt around LLM responses.
Google appears set to rebrand Pixel's Magic Cue as Gemini 'Proactive Assistance,' folding the phone's ambient, context-aware suggestions under the Gemini umbrella.
How XREAL's new $299 a01 glasses stack up against the rest of the lineup — the cheapest entry yet into wearable-display glasses, aimed at movies and games.
PrismML released Bonsai 27B, claiming it's the first model of that size that actually runs on an iPhone — a push to move frontier-class on-device AI onto phone silicon.
The first watchOS 27 public beta brings the rebuilt Siri AI to Apple Watch, along with a smarter app grid and widgets — Apple Intelligence arriving on the wrist surface.
Apple's iOS 27 public beta is out, giving iPhone users their first open shot at the rebuilt Siri AI plus broad performance upgrades.
An activist group hijacked London bus-stop ad panels with spoof Meta Glasses campaigns, using the brand's own visual language to attack always-on camera wearables.
